title: What got you interested in game design/development?

posts.author: Litningman06
posts.body: Just like the title says! I’d never really thought about making games before a few years ago, when I was checking out Toby Fox’s Earthbound Halloween Hack. That night, I woke up in the middle of the night and thought about all the little details that I loved about that hack, and eventually came to the conclusion that I wanted to make an RPG. Five failed projects and one finished one later, here I am, asking you all this question.

posts.author: zerobeat032
posts.body:
back when I was a LOT younger... I had a comic book idea. but I kinda suck at drawing stuff that would work for an actual comic. one summer after a breakup, I messed with RPG Maker XP for like a solid month. I wasn't trying to do anything series tho. It wasn't until 5 years ago that randomly watching my friend stream his art process that it hit me, turn the comic into a game.
sooo... it wasn't necessarily any game that got me interested so much as I wanted to tell the story of my comic really badly and was crazy enough to make it a game lol.

posts.author: raymadeit
posts.body: My older brother and I LOVED making up stories when we were younger. This eventually led down the RPG Maker rabbit hole a little over 15 years ago when I was in middle school. Back then we were using RPG Maker XP and we were just having fun with it. Loved everything about it. That's how I originally learned how to program and is how I make a living today.

posts.author: shawesomesauce
posts.body: For me I've always really liked drawing, writing, storytelling, animating, etc. They all became hobbies of mine and I wanted a way to put them all together, and apparently making a video game was the solution lol

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
As a kid, I made up games with my friends and little brother, including many iffy variations of Chess, and many gamified stories.
It wasn't until I found the devlog series from the youtube channel Echo607 that I really considered making video games specifically, and even then it wasn't until after the poorly planned "game development club" at my high school fell into pieces that I seriously took the idea of RPG Maker into consideration.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
I used to play a lot of free games.  This was pre VXAce release and a lot were FF clones, though there are some gems from that era.  I often thought: This is terrible. Even I could do better than this."
Then one day I thought: "Well, in that case why don't you try?"
So I did.

posts.author: Heian
posts.body:
Tried drawing a webcomic, could barely get past the first panel.
Tried writing a novel, could only write out of context climatic scenes.
But gamedevving? I have sprites and art to save myself from drawing a new picture for every scene and from having too much or too little of descriptions.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
For me it started in the way back time...the mid 80s...when computers where first being introduced to schools around the country. When they didn't even have internal hard drives and everything was saved on "floppy" disks.
My high school got some computers and I took a VERY basic intro to computers class. One of my friends and I would go to the computer lab and try to draw things on the screen using X plot and Y plot to draw line by line. We would trace a picture onto a transparency, tape the transparency to the monitor, and then plot line by line to trace what was on the transparency.
We were also big into D&D so we tried making very simple text-based games. Like you are walking down a corridor and come to an intersection with 3 branches. Which way do you go? And very basic fighting.
We didn't make much progress, but even back then, I wanted to make a D&D type game of my own. Because back then, I didn't even know that games like that for computers existed. My small town of 1,200 people didn't have a computer store or anything like it.
I didn't know that games like Wizardry 1 were already out since 1981. I didn't get my own first computer and my own first CRPG until 1990. I bought Eye of the Beholder and then Wizardry 6. And I was hooked.
My desire to make my own game basically sat on the back burner and I spent almost 40 years writing instead. Then I finally decided I wanted to try something different than writing and see if I could learn enough to make my own game. Not sure why I didn't decide that earlier.
So a couple of years ago, I did my research, discovered that RPG Maker had been out since forever, and I ended up deciding to buy MZ. I haven't looked back and I definitely don't regret my decision.
I just wish I had started my game dev journey about 30 years ago.

posts.author: MAH1RO
posts.body:
At first it was 3D design for me. I did it for nearly all my years in school very actively after a friend showed me the 3D program "Blender". But the first game Ideas I had were way too much for me and my friends to handle (basically all were fantasy RPGs and stuff like this). We had already quite a bunch of very nice objects and landscape, but it was just a small part of what we needed. So in the end we did not continue it when we realized what it really means to make a game of this scale. But the creative process was fun.
Then last year I just saw the RPG Maker MV on sale on Steam and I remembered that even before I started 3D design back in school (when I was only ~12 years old) another friend showed me one of the old RPG-Maker engines and we tried to make a game with it (it failed horribly xD). But now with 15 years more life experience and a newer RPG-Maker engine I wanted to try it again. Especially because its a really basic and simple engine but enough for what I want to do. It took me some time to find all the Plugins and adapt the base engine to what I need, but I like it.

posts.author: daMooseNeo
posts.body:
I've been around it a long, long, time, lol~
"Game Design" for me ends up covering a wide swath. As a kid in the early 90s I'd wanted to design my own NES/SNES games, laid out a number on paper. Got into Basic computer programming languages, wrote a ton there. Got into Gameboy ROM hacking around 99/2000, learned a lot about assembly, spent a lot of time hacking apart Pokemon Red/Blue. Got into 3D game design, client/server architecture, built some small MMO-type engines that ran on dial-up
Spent a lot of time on table-top game design, making some small adventure board games before moving on to TCG designs, publishing a small game in 2004 while I was in college...lots of tabletop design since then, indie RPG and d20-based releases for 3rd edition, Pathfinder, Starfinder, some design work for 5E adventures...
I ended up parlaying all of that into opening a game store, so that's taken a LOT of time away from other things, but the store's been running for 17 years now and keeps things going so I don't complain
There was a licensing dust-up around the d20 license and the Open Game License last year that fubared an in-progress design of mine and I put it on the backburner. In 2020 I ended up nabbing a cheap copy of MV to pass some time and late last year I decided I'd dig that out and adapt my in-progress setting into an RPG Maker game~ Is a lot more setting and system than it is story, but I'm rather proud of some support software I wrote to test various plot generating rules/algorithms, and I'm adapting those to generate quests for the RPGM build. Its going to be fun

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
posts.body: I like makin' art for art's sake and I like makin' music for music's sake, but iunno...sometimes a clear goal for both is nice.

posts.author: Cythera
posts.body:
I was complaining about a mobile gacha game a friend and I both played. I went on a rant about the RNG and the game mechanics and the near-forced metas if you wanted to do well in. Eventually I proclaimed I could make a better game.
He sent me a copy of MV on Steam and said, prove it. And here I am.
For the record, I thoroughly believe my game is better. And yet...I still play that gacha game

posts.author: BloodyKun
posts.body:
Interesting to see where so many others here are coming from.  Don’t think I have anything as interesting or clear cut, but I’ll try to be concise.
Had started gaming myself with my older brother on the SNES, games like Super Mario World, Donkey Kong Country, Beavis and Butthead of which my dad saw nothing wrong with despite our mother being adamant about refusing it lol.  Later on, Street Fighter 2, Uniracers, Killer Instinct, other little odds and ends.  So I’ve been gaming since at least 3-4 years old.
But then the N64 came along, introduced to 3D with Donkey Kong 64, and that and Kirby 64 were some favorites for a good long while til a friend introduced me to Zelda with Ocarina of Time.  With a name like that, I wasn’t so sure about playing something so “girly” only to be proven wrong and have it be one of my favorite series ever since, even if it was somehow more daunting to my young mind than DK64, gargantuan collectathon its known as.  But I think Wind Waker a bit later became my absolute favorite, perhaps in part being the first game I ever finished without any help from my brother, who had sorta moved on to other things with friends while I’d always been a bit too shy and anxious to do the same.
Much later I got my first job going on 16, Wii was great and all but got tired of waiting for new games, and went ahead and bought a 360 to see what stuff there was other than Nintendo.  My brother and I had tried PS1 and 2, fine stuff, but not much outside of GTA interested us.  So it was quite a new experience, getting into Halo 3 and meeting new friends who I’d game with for many years to come, and would leave a lasting impression on me as we drifted apart.  I had no idea online multiplayer could be so fun, even the dumber games like Avatar Paintball of all things, and it’s made it hard for me to go back and try some more.  Thankfully I’ve made some newer friends who will chill and play stuff like Among Us (despite me not being able to lie very convincingly) or Jackbox stuff (which ends up very raunchy) and lately silly stuff like Crab Chsmpions.  Kinda miss more involved games like Halo but casual stuff can be fun, too.
But the real big deal was No More Heroes, when that released on the Wii…it seemed to open up a whole new world to me, not only with Grasshopper’s other games but those that took their stories more seriously, even if many might be silly on the surface.  Deadly Premonition, Yakuza, Nier, even going back to look at older games, especially horror ones I had been too afraid to play first hand like Silent Hill 2, Rule of Rose, even Chulip disturbed me a bit, but I think I gained a new appreciation for storytelling after having played NMH and subsequently Killer7.  And even getting to actually know people like Swery, really down to earth guy despite the language barrier, having made such great games I enjoyed, really look up to him.  I think that’s the final push it took me to look at my art, much as I enjoy writing and drawing, to want to use those skills I have to make something anyone can interact with on a deeper level.  I love books and shows and movies and all, but I simply feel games are my favorite medium, and I want to one day be able to touch others’ minds as mine has been, to inspire others to express themselves fully to the best of their abilities.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Growing up I always wanted to be the idea guy, well actually the idea guy of idea guys...like a guy who tells other people to have ideas based on my ideas and then evaluate those ideas and then make other people make those ideas a reality. (That would still be my favorite role.)
I always kind of wanted to make a game, but didn't have any skills or talents, nor the passion to learn any skills. Then one day when my mind was working a bit more dynamically, I came up with a couple of plot points and character ideas. Then I decided that I will make a game with some simple engine like RPG Maker. I decided that it will be a visual novel, because ****, I don't have the energy or interest to make any real game mechanics. And I wrote an epic plot and put together some simple minigames with rpg maker events.
And that's how I made a game.

posts.author: TheoAllen
posts.body:
Back in the day, making custom maps and scenarios in Age of Empire 2 and Starcraft 1 was fun.
I made a stupid story while I was at it.
I thought I liked game dev, but in reality, I just like the engineering part of the game dev.

posts.author: Popoto_milk
posts.body:
The catalyst for my interest was the desire to learn art. Taking the steps to learn that was when I began toying with the idea of making games.  After all, if you're not limited to something like "I can't draw" it really opens up what you can do. And I really like stories so games(VNs specifically) were appealing.
But what actually made me do something about making games was one experience. I played a game and was really wowed by it. Decided to check out the engine since I didn't know too much about it. And that's actually what brought me here.

posts.author: BlueMoonCorp
posts.body:
As bad as this sounds I'm not even gonna lie..... it more or less began (and sort of continues) with Envy. I grew up without any talent worth taking note of outside my imagination. I was also very much into video games. I used to like writing stories whenever I had the chance and would always think "why am I even doing this? Who's ever going to read this and say 'oh, I bet we can make this into a video game'". That kind of stuff USUALLY only happens in tv shows and movies. so for a while just kind of stopped.
Fast forwarding a few years later, when someone told me about rpg maker I kinda jumped on it in an instant. As someone who once again can't draw, make music, sing, and monotone unexpressive voice (meaning I also wasn't very confident in voice acting) I found this as one way to get my creative ideas at LEAST going. I knew at most I could pay people to assist me in departments that I would fail. So far other than a few ost's I have created 8+ hours of gameplay all by myself with no help and personally I think it's going very well. It's almost complete actually.
Now here comes the part about envy and it gets really strange. Dont laugh!
Anyway, the whole envy thing is also surprisingly keeping me going. I don't know why or how but it started when we got a smash reveal for Joker in smash bros. I remember thinking.... hey.....how nice it must feel for a character you created to be invited to something so.... spectacular. Even games like Undertale made me feel self-conscious about what I wasn't able to do, not to mention Toby essentially got to make stuff for Nintendo (I'm not blaming anyone but myself of course).
I was never envious to the point I wished other people's work would fail, just more so that I wished some random miracle would happen and I suddenly got blessed with the same kind of luck and or talent. Point is, I'm not like that anymore but I do still feel a bit of envy. Instead of looking at it as a bad thing, I look at it as something to push me to do what I can. Now I've gone to wanting my game to make a name for itself once it's finished. I genuinely want people to enjoy something I created maybe even gather a small fanbase. Yeah, praise would be nice too (let's be honest, a lot of people do want that) but it's also because I want to show that you don't need all the talent in the world to make something people like. You just need to invest the love and effort into what you create. If it's good and it makes even a few people happy, I'll consider it a success. If it's bad... well I'll take what I learn and fix what I can because I invested time and love into my game and I want it to be the best it can be.
Sorry for the life story. XD

posts.author: cuebitcrush
posts.body:
I only started looking into game design once I had to figure out what I was going to study after high school. I was super into Hollow Knight at the time and I liked the art style so much that I figured I wanted to do something like it in the future, in regards to making environment art or game assets.
I love storytelling but I'm no good at coding and I've never really had any fully fleshed out stories that I could adapt into something more polished so I never thought I'd touch game development, but on a whim I bought RM2K3 on sale last year and started following a few tutorials with it. In a professional sense I'd still rather make assets than participate in development, and I ended up choosing not to pursue a degree in game design, but I've been having fun making things on my own time!
